truths.CP2:
SELECT COUNT(*) - (
  SELECT COUNT(*)
  FROM (
    -- one row per different line of 2010
    SELECT DISTINCT invoice, stock_code, description, quantity, invoice_date, price, customer_id, country
    FROM invoice_lines
    WHERE invoice_date >= TIMESTAMP '2010-01-01'
      AND invoice_date < TIMESTAMP '2011-01-01'
  ) AS d
)
FROM invoice_lines
WHERE invoice_date >= TIMESTAMP '2010-01-01'
  AND invoice_date < TIMESTAMP '2011-01-01'
truths.CP4:
SELECT ROUND(SUM(d.quantity * d.price), 2)
FROM (
  -- one row per different product line of 2010
  SELECT DISTINCT invoice, stock_code, description, quantity, invoice_date, price, customer_id, country
  FROM invoice_lines
  WHERE invoice_date >= TIMESTAMP '2010-01-01'
    AND invoice_date < TIMESTAMP '2011-01-01'
    AND substring(stock_code, 1, 1) BETWEEN '0' AND '9'
) AS d

CP1.explanation: A line with no customer ID is still a sale, so dropping it cuts revenue; the customer ID matters only when the question is about customers, and the cancellations are the invoices that start with C.

CP5.explanation: One year of months cannot tell a seasonal dip from a loss of customers, and revenue is not a count of customers; the same month a year earlier and the customers per month can.
